summary: Cape Town's Atlantic Seaboard is among the best-secured expat zones on the continent. Sea Point, Camps Bay, and the Southern Suburbs are genuinely livable with strong security infrastructure. The city's challenge is stark geographic inequality: the Cape Flats townships experience a gang violence crisis that is structurally separate from where visitors and expats actually operate. Knowing which Cape Town you're in makes all the difference.
dataSource: US State Dept, UK FCO, Numbeo 2025, South African Police Service (SAPS)

ukFco.summary: South Africa has a high level of crime including violent crime. Take care throughout the country. The main risks are mugging, bag-snatching, carjacking, and home robbery.

currentAlerts: Gang violence in Cape Flats is concentrated in Khayelitsha, Mitchells Plain, Gugulethu, and Nyanga. These areas are geographically and socially separate from the Atlantic Seaboard and Southern Suburbs where visitors operate.
Table Mountain muggings of tourists ongoing in 2024-2025. Hike only in groups or with a guide. Never solo.
Load shedding (power outages): when electricity cuts, home alarms and neighborhood CCTV go offline. Know your load shedding schedule and heighten security awareness during those windows.
May 2025 advisory update: load shedding specifically flagged as a security multiplier.
safetyTips: Never hike Table Mountain, Lion's Head, or Signal Hill alone. Only in groups with other people visible. Muggings are targeted and planned.
Keep all doors locked while driving. Carjacking at traffic lights is extremely common. Engage locks before you stop.
Do not stop if strangers gesture at your car or flag you down on the road.
Use only Uber or Bolt. Never metered street taxis alone at night.
Home security: electric fence plus armed response is the standard for expats in Cape Town.
During load shedding windows, heighten security awareness. Deadbolts over electronic locks.
Tourist areas in the CBD (V&A Waterfront, long streets) are relatively safe during the day. Clear out before dark.

To report a crime or call police in Cape Town, dial 10111 (South African Police Service). For general emergencies including medical and fire, dial 10177 (ambulance) or 112 (national emergency from mobile). Cape Town City Emergency Services: 021 480 7700.
If you have subscribed to a home or vehicle security company (ADT, Chubb, Fidelity), their armed response number is typically faster than SAPS. Save your security company's number.
US citizens contact the U.S. Consulate General Cape Town for emergency consular assistance at +27 21 702 7300. UK nationals contact the British Consulate General Cape Town at +27 21 405 2400.
Enroll in the US Embassy Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at step.state.gov before your trip to receive automatic security alerts for South Africa.
